sections.title: Proposed project
sections.value: QA Control Review for cell MR-17

sections.title: Business need
sections.value: MR-17 is down due to command authorization and retired test control issues. Clear records are needed to control procedures and preserve evidence for future decisions.

sections.title: Expected value and beneficiaries
sections.value:
-QA, Engineering, and Production Operations
-The review gives QA and Engineering a traceable record they can use to investigate further, and give Operations a solid reason to ask for future fixes. It wont fix the robot right now. but it makes sure future decisions are backed by evidence

sections.title: Included work
sections.value: Reviewing command ownership, managing retired tests, starting up evidence preservation, and delivering a final QA report to Operations,   QA, and engineering

sections.title: Excluded work
sections.value: The review does not authorize a restart, software changes, altered original records, a replacement robot, or a vendor choice.

sections.title: Technical feasibility
sections.value: Yes, read only exports and current tools support the review. W02-S04, staff only need read only access to command log exports.

sections.title: Operational feasibility
sections.value: Record custodians, QA Engineering, and Operations staff will need to confirm their availability to ensure they can fit locating, reviewing, and receiving these records around their duties.

sections.title: Cost and resource feasibility
sections.value:
Base cost of $2,820 fits under the $3,000 limit, but the range of $2,350-$3,525 could exceed it if costs rise (W02-S05)
Software changes, new equipment, and vendors are excluded.

sections.title: Schedule feasibility
sections.value: 8- business day plan fits within the 10-day limit, but the 48 total staff hours represent total effort across teams, not 48 elapsed hours. Engineering work cannot start until day 4 because it depends on receiving the data exports scheduled for days 1-3

sections.title: Known constraints
sections.value:
Budget limit - $3,000 Max
Schedule Limit - 10 Business day Max
Access & Safety - Read only data access/ MR-17 stays powered off w/no software edits or physical test allowed

sections.title: Risks and assumptions
sections.value:
- Data exports from records custodians will arrive on schedule by day 3 
- Late exports or QA shift reassignments would delay Engineering start date on day 4 and risk pushing the project beyond the 10 business day limit 
- Elias, Robotics systems engineer & Records custodian lead should verify export timelines before work begins

sections.title: Success measures and evidence
sections.value: Delivery is checked by making sure Nia and Elias review all 3 deliverables. Value is based on the measured baseline of 6 retrieval request taking 60 mins total, while any future time savings are just targets that need to be measured.

sections.title: Rationale and conditions
sections.value: The review fits within the $3,000 and 10 day limit (SRC-01). It gives QA and Engineering clear records to find root causes and gives Operations a solid basis to request future work (SRC-02). This does not guarantee fixing the robot right now.

sections.title: Next authorization or information step
sections.value: The sponsor should make the final decision to authorize the project. Before starting, Elias and the records custodian lead must confirm export schedules and team availability.
